title.narrative: LINKS: Integration of Indigenous and local knowledge in environmental policies

description.narrative: Indigenous Peoples and local communities possess valuable knowledge about the environment such as in ocean and water conservation, including sustainable fishing and coastal management. Despite this deep knowledge, their expertise is often overlooked in decision-making processes. UNESCO-LINKS seeks to bridge this gap by facilitating knowledge exchange among policymakers, scientists, and Indigenous knowledge holders. Using a multiple evidence-based approach and Indigenous knowledge exchange and dialogue workshops, it aims to integrate Indigenous perspective and their holistic view into environmental policies, including in ocean and water conservation policies. It will also support safeguarding and transmission of this traditional knowledge, including through an approach which targets the preservation of Indigenous Peoples rights, culture and languages. The initiative aligns with the key decades, including the International Water Action Decade, the International Decade for Ocean Science, and the International Decade of Indigenous Languages.
